meta.title: Why Pascal blamed all our misery on one thing

beats.text: Pascal thought he had found the root of nearly all our unhappiness.
"All of humanity's problems," he wrote, "stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone."
Left alone with no distraction, we feel our smallness, our boredom, our mortality rise up.
So we flee. Into noise, into busyness, into anything that keeps us from our own company.
We call it entertainment. Pascal called it diversion — a way of not thinking about ourselves.
It works, until it doesn't. The silence we run from is always waiting at the end of the noise.
Try it tonight. One room. No screen. Just you — and see what you have been running from.

source_note: Quote: Pensées, trans. W. F. Trotter (public domain).
